checks: The common left bases −h, including h=0, cancel. The right bases h+1 in the even chain and h in the odd chain produce exactly the paired terms at t+βh and the final core at t+β(m+1). The identity also gives just the core when m=0.

Each nested-triangle difference is the ordinary area of the selected annulus. These annuli and the core partition RT up to area-null boundaries, and their thresholds are all no larger than the final threshold. This proves the coarse lower comparison without counting annuli twice.

For interior a, the two proper tail formulas follow from the intercept fractions; their threshold derivative magnitudes meet at 2r/a at the lower-to-upper branch transition. For a=1/2 the derivative magnitude is at most 4r, and for a=1 it is at most 2r. The continuous clipped tails are therefore globally 4R-Lipschitz when r=R.

The central point has equal barycentric coordinates 1/3 and the cutting plane passes through it. The accepted centroid-depth formula gives the normalization F_R(t)≥4R²/9, hence the coarse bound with error 4Rβ(m+1).

For s>0 and a∈[2/3,1), varying r yields density zero, then affine slope 2/(2a−1), then a constant, with matching values at both radial knots. The a=1 formula 2(r−s)_+ yields the endpoint directly. Thus the annular derivative loss bound holds almost everywhere.

Apply the radial Lipschitz bound separately with threshold increment βh at annulus h and β(m+1) at the core. The weighted radial drops telescope to ∑_h r_h. Zero terminal radii contribute zero and do not create a derivative singularity for s>0.

Original 5e6e53a58ea7a59b §6 gives the coarse telescope and a6778097fd0174ca Lemmas 1–2 give the refined first-radius-moment bound. The further moment substitution in the latter source is outside the stated result.

dependencies.hypotheses: Take the scaled standard triangle and its centroid (R/3,R/3), with three barycentrics equal to 1/3≤1/2. The normalized depth is 4/9, so the own tail in units of |T| is at least 4R²/9.

The accepted proof contains the individual triangle-tail formulas. It has no paired-chain difference identity or radius-Lipschitz comparison for its annular densities.
